name: SR 12

planets.name: c
planets.note: Planetary-mass companion (~11-14 Mjup) at 8.7 arcsec (980 au) from the SR 12 AB binary; imaged by Kuzuhara et al. 2011, who also demonstrated common proper motion over 10 yr of astrometry. One of the widest known planetary-mass companions and the first imaged around a binary host.

images.wavelength_label: 0.88 mm continuum (circumplanetary disk around SR 12 c)
images.credit: Wu et al. 2022, Fig. 1 (crop; SR 12 c panel)

paper.title: ALMA Discovery of a Disk around the Planetary-mass Companion SR 12 c
Ultraviolet Imaging of SR 12 c with HST/WFC3: Accretion and Variability of a Giant Planet
A Mid-infrared Study of Directly Imaged Planetary-mass Companions Using Archival Spitzer/IRAC

notes: SR 12 AB is a weak-line T Tauri binary (separation 0.21 arcsec / ~24 au) in the rho Ophiuchi star-forming region. Its wide (980 au) planetary-mass companion SR 12 c was imaged by Kuzuhara et al. 2011; ALMA Band 7 (0.88 mm) imaging by Wu et al. 2022 detected an unresolved (<5 au) circumplanetary dust disk around SR 12 c, the first submillimeter detection of a CPD around a wide planetary-mass companion, with dust mass comparable to the PDS 70 c CPD.
